about: Fresh, unlabelled Scripts for the order-bias eval (training/order_bias.py). Written for BandCraft AI on 2026-10-01 on prompts not used in the Gold Set, spanning weak to strong writing. They carry no bands on purpose: the eval measures whether Gemini's bands change when only the prompt's ordering changes, which needs no ground truth. scripts.prompt: Some people think that working from home is better for employees, while others believe it is better to work in an office. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
scripts.script:
Nowadays many people is working from home because of the internet. Some people think it is better and some people think office is better. I will discuss both of them.

First, working from home have many advantage. You dont need to go to the office every day so you save time and money for the bus or the petrol. Also you can wear what you want and you can make your coffee when you want. My sister work from home and she say she is more happy now. She can stay with her children and she cook lunch for them.

But office also have good things. In the office you can talk with your colleagues and if you have problem they help you quickly. At home sometimes the internet is not working and you cannot do your work. Also at home there is many distractions like TV and phone and children which is making noise. Some people become lazy at home because nobody control them.

In my opinion, working from home is better for most people. Because it save time and people are more relax. But the company must give them good computer and internet. Also maybe they can go to office one or two day in a week to meet the colleagues, so it is not boring.

In conclusion, both have advantages and disadvantages but I think working from home is more better for employees today and in the future more people will work from home.

scripts.prompt: Some people think that working from home is better for employees, while others believe it is better to work in an office. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
scripts.script:
The rapid spread of remote working has reopened an old question about where people do their best work. While the office still offers benefits that are hard to replicate online, I believe that, for most employees, working from home is the better arrangement, provided it is not total.

Advocates of the office point first to collaboration. Problems that would take a dozen emails to resolve can often be settled in a two-minute conversation at someone's desk, and junior staff in particular learn a great deal simply by overhearing how experienced colleagues handle difficult clients. There is also a psychological argument: a physical commute, however tiresome, marks a clear boundary between work and private life, and many remote workers report that this boundary dissolves when the kitchen table doubles as a desk.

On the other hand, the case for home working is compelling. Eliminating the daily commute returns hours to employees each week, time that can be spent on rest, exercise or family. Remote work also widens access to jobs for parents, people with disabilities and those who live far from major cities, who might otherwise be excluded altogether. Moreover, many employees find that they concentrate better without the constant interruptions of an open-plan office, which suggests that the supposed productivity advantage of the workplace is far from universal.

In my view, the strongest solution combines the two. A hybrid model, in which teams meet in person on agreed days for collaboration and mentoring but work remotely the rest of the time, preserves the genuine strengths of the office while giving employees the flexibility that clearly improves their wellbeing.

In conclusion, although offices remain valuable for teamwork and training, home working better serves the needs of most employees, especially when it is balanced with regular face-to-face contact.

scripts.prompt: International tourism has brought enormous benefits to many places. At the same time, there is concern about its impact on local inhabitants and the environment. Do the disadvantages of international tourism outweigh the advantages? Write at least 250 words.
scripts.script:
International tourism has grown very fast in the last decades, and many countries now depend on it. However, some people worry that tourists damage the environment and change the life of local people. In my opinion, the advantages are still bigger than the disadvantages, although governments need to manage tourism carefully.

The main advantage of tourism is economic. Tourists spend money in hotels, restaurants and shops, which creates jobs for local people, especially in regions where there are few other industries. For example, many small islands in Asia earn most of their income from visitors. Tourism also helps cultural exchange, because people from different countries can learn about each other's traditions and become more tolerant.

On the other hand, there are clear disadvantages. Popular places like Venice or Barcelona become very crowded, and the prices of houses increase so much that local residents cannot afford to live in the city centre. In addition, tourism can harm nature. Planes produce a lot of pollution, and in some beaches the coral reefs have been damaged by too many divers and boats.

Despite these problems, I believe they can be reduced with good policies. Governments can limit the number of visitors in sensitive areas, introduce tourist taxes and use this money to protect the environment and build affordable housing. Bhutan, for example, charges visitors a daily fee to control numbers.

In conclusion, although international tourism causes overcrowding and environmental damage, its economic and cultural benefits are greater, as long as it is planned and controlled properly.

scripts.prompt: In many countries, older people find it difficult to use modern technology. What are the reasons for this? What can be done to help them? Write at least 250 words.
scripts.script:
Modern technology such as smartphones, online banking and self-service machines has become part of everyday life. However, many older people struggle to use these devices. This essay will explain the main reasons for this problem and suggest some solutions.

One reason is that older people did not grow up with digital technology. Unlike young people, who learn to use computers at school, many elderly people only met these devices late in life, so the logic of menus, icons and passwords feels unfamiliar to them. Another reason is physical. As people age, their eyesight and hearing often become weaker, and small buttons or text on a phone screen can be very hard to read. Finally, some older people are afraid of making mistakes, for example sending money to the wrong person, so they avoid using technology at all.

There are several ways to solve this problem. Firstly, local councils and libraries could organise free classes where volunteers teach basic skills step by step and at a slow pace. Secondly, companies should design simpler products with larger text, fewer options and clear instructions. Some phone makers already offer an 'easy mode', and this should become more common. Thirdly, families can play an important role; grandchildren can spend time showing their grandparents how to make video calls or pay bills online.

In conclusion, older people have difficulty with technology mainly because of lack of experience, physical changes and fear of mistakes. With patient teaching, better design and support from their families, they can become more confident and independent users.

scripts.prompt: Some people believe that the best way to reduce traffic congestion is to make public transport free. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Write at least 250 words.
scripts.script:
As cities grow, traffic congestion has become one of the most visible failures of urban planning, and the idea of abolishing fares on buses and trains has gained popularity as a seemingly simple cure. While free public transport can help, I disagree that it is the most effective way to reduce congestion.

The attraction of the policy is clear. Removing fares lowers the cost of travel for everyone, particularly low-income households, and can persuade some drivers to leave their cars at home. Tallinn, which introduced free transport for residents in 2013, did see a rise in passenger numbers, and there are genuine social benefits in making mobility affordable for all.

However, the evidence suggests that price is rarely the main reason people drive. Commuters choose cars because they are faster, more comfortable or more reliable than the alternatives, and a free bus that is overcrowded, infrequent or stuck in the same traffic jam offers little incentive to switch. Indeed, studies of fare-free schemes have found that many new passengers were previously walking or cycling rather than driving, so congestion barely changed. Free transport also deprives operators of revenue that could otherwise fund the improvements that really attract drivers.

A more effective approach combines better services with measures that make driving less attractive. Dedicated bus lanes, frequent and punctual trains, and well-connected routes address the real reasons people avoid public transport, while congestion charges, as in London and Stockholm, directly reduce the number of cars in city centres and raise money for further investment.

In conclusion, although free public transport has social value, it is not the best solution to congestion; improving quality and pricing road use are likely to achieve far more.

scripts.prompt:
The table below shows the percentage of electricity generated from different sources in one country in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

Data (% of electricity generated, 2005 then 2025):
Coal: 55, 20
Natural gas: 25, 30
Nuclear: 15, 15
Wind: 3, 22
Solar: 2, 13
scripts.script:
The table compares the proportion of electricity produced from five sources in a country in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, coal lost its dominant position over the period, while renewable sources, especially wind, grew significantly. Natural gas became the largest single source by 2025.

In 2005, coal was by far the most important source, generating more than half of the country's electricity (55%). Natural gas accounted for a quarter, and nuclear power provided 15%. Wind and solar were very minor, at only 3% and 2% respectively.

By 2025, the picture had changed considerably. The share of coal fell sharply to just 20%, which was lower than natural gas, whose share rose slightly to 30%. The biggest increase was in wind power, which grew from 3% to 22%, making it the second largest source. Solar energy also increased a lot, reaching 13%. In contrast, the proportion from nuclear power stayed the same at 15%.

In summary, the country moved away from coal towards gas and renewable energy during these twenty years.

scripts.prompt:
Your neighbour has been making a lot of noise late at night. Write a letter to your neighbour. In your letter:
- explain what the problem is
- describe how it is affecting you
- suggest what could be done about it
Write at least 150 words. You do NOT need to write any addresses. Begin your letter as follows: Dear ...,
scripts.script:
Dear Mr Collins,

I hope you are well. I am writing about something that has been worrying me for a few weeks, and I hope we can sort it out in a friendly way.

Recently there has been quite loud music and voices coming from your flat late at night, usually after midnight and sometimes until two or three in the morning. I understand that you may have guests or be watching films, but the walls in our building are thin and the sound carries very easily into my bedroom.

As a result, I have had real trouble sleeping. I start work at seven, so I have been arriving tired and finding it hard to concentrate, and my young son has also been woken up several times.

Would it be possible to keep the volume lower after eleven o'clock on weeknights? Perhaps you could also use headphones late in the evening. If there is a special occasion, just let me know in advance and I will not mind.

Thank you for understanding.

Best regards,
Samal Nurlanova
